title: Indonesia's internet use is widespread, but the device ecology remains mobile-first with low computer and fixed-line ownership
source_unit: BPS-Statistics Indonesia, Telecommunication Statistics in Indonesia 2024
geography: Indonesia; national population, households, and internet users represented by Susenas 2024

observations.period: 2023-2024; national internet use and mobile-phone ownership

denominator.unit: Indonesia population represented by BPS national estimates; internet and device indicators use their stated Susenas denominators

internet_access_2023.unit: percent of population accessing the internet

internet_access_2024.unit: percent of population accessing the internet

mobile_cellular_phone_ownership_2024.unit: percent of population owning or using a mobile cellular phone

mobile_cellular_phone_ownership_2023.unit: percent of population owning or using a mobile cellular phone

mechanism.value: Internet use is expanding alongside mobile ownership, making mobile devices the primary gateway to digital culture, sociality, and commerce for a large population; the aggregate does not reveal quality, affordability, or depth of use

observations.method: BPS annual telecommunications publication drawing on the National Socio-Economic Survey (Susenas), with internet-use indicators reported for 2023 and 2024.
observations.uncertainty: Internet access is a recent-use indicator and does not measure frequency, data volume, device quality, bandwidth, cultural use, or household-level access conditions.
observations.subgroup: Indonesia's national population represented by BPS Susenas estimates.
observations.counterinterpretation: Rising internet use may reflect multiple users sharing devices, low-intensity access, or administrative and survey changes rather than equal digital optionality.

observations.period: 2024; household technology ownership and internet-user device access

denominator.unit: Indonesia population and households represented by BPS Susenas 2024 estimates

household_computer_ownership.unit: percent of households owning or controlling a computer

household_fixed_line_phone_ownership.unit: percent of households owning or controlling a fixed-line telephone

mobile_cellular_as_internet_access_devic.unit: percent of internet users using a mobile cellular device to access the internet

laptop_as_internet_access_device.unit: percent of internet users using a laptop to access the internet

mechanism.value: The Indonesian digital-consumer stack is overwhelmingly handset-based: almost all internet users use mobile cellular devices, while computer ownership and fixed-line telephony are minority conditions

observations.method: BPS Susenas 2024 household-ownership and internet-user device indicators; device percentages may be multiple response.
observations.uncertainty: The measures do not identify smartphone quality, shared-device use, screen size, data cost, computer availability at work or school, or the activities performed on each device.
observations.subgroup: Indonesian households and internet users represented by the 2024 Susenas survey.
observations.counterinterpretation: Handset-first access can be an adaptive and sufficient pathway for many activities; low computer ownership does not necessarily imply low digital participation.

denominator.unit: population internet users represented by BPS Susenas 2024 estimates; location measures allow multiple responses

internet_access_at_own_home.unit: percent of internet users accessing at their own home

internet_access_public_places.unit: percent of internet users accessing in public places

internet_access_in_moving_vehicle.unit: percent of internet users accessing in a moving vehicle

internet_access_commercial_location.unit: percent of internet users accessing in commercial locations

mechanism.value: Home remains the dominant access location, but public and mobile-mobility access are material secondary layers, suggesting that digital cultural and consumer participation can move across household, public, and transit spaces

observations.method: BPS Susenas 2024 internet-location indicators; responses can exceed 100% because users may access at multiple locations.
observations.uncertainty: Location of access does not measure quality, privacy, time burden, cost, or what users do online; the denominator is internet users rather than the full population.
observations.subgroup: Indonesian population aged 5 years and above accessing the internet in the reference period, as defined by BPS tables.
observations.counterinterpretation: High home access may reflect mobile use inside the home rather than fixed broadband, and public-place access may be incidental or low intensity.

related_sources.claim: BPS publication documents Susenas-based internet penetration, mobile ownership, fixed-line and computer ownership, and telecommunications context.
BPS statistical table provides internet-access device shares for computer, laptop, mobile cellular, and other devices in 2024.

boundary: This record adds Indonesian evidence on internet penetration, mobile/computer/fixed-line device ecology, and access locations. It does not measure cultural participation, platform behavior, digital quality, data affordability, household inequality, or causal consumer effects.
